title: Kendrick Perkins Shares Message For Ja Morant Ahead Of Grizzlies Contest

 Kendrick Perkins hypes up Ja Morant ahead of facing his former team, the Memphis Grizzlies
 by Soumik Bhattacharya | Oct 30, 2026 | 2 min Ja Morant receives message from Kendrick Perkins ahead of the Portland-Memphis game · Credits: via X Global Nba For nearly seven seasons, Ja Morant’s name had been synonymous with the Memphis Grizzlies. The 27-year-old had rightfully established himself as the franchise's cornerstone, even leading it to a conference semifinals run in the 2021-22 season. With the Grizzlies, Morant won the NBA Rookie of the Year and NBA Improved Player of the Year awards and earned two All-Star selections. 
 However, that association and success soon faded after Morant’s initial seasons with the Grizzlies. Following a slump in the 27-year-old’s career, Morant was eventually traded to the Portland Trail Blazers ahead of the 2026-27 season.
 Now, as Morant prepares to take on the Grizzlies for the first time since that trade, former NBA champion Kendrick Perkins has a powerful message for the former. 
 “If I’m Ja, I’m gonna make the Grizzlies smell my cologne,” Perkins said via NBA on ESPN. “Hey Ja, listen, this organization gave up on you when you was at your lowest point. They said, you know what, we can’t even deal with it. You’re not good enough for us to continue to deal with everything and the baggage that you was bringing to the table at the time. So now you make them pay.” 
 "This organization gave up on you ... now you make them pay."
@KendrickPerkins has a message for Ja Morant ahead of facing the Grizzlies 👀 https://t.co/TsyPJwAyap
— NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) October 29, 2026 
 Ja Morant’s second half with the Memphis Grizzlies was a shadow of the start the 27-year-old had with the franchise. The two-time NBA All-Star’s stint was plagued by injuries, including hip, hamstring, and UCL issues. Notably, Morant also played just 79 games across his three seasons with the franchise, which raised questions about his availability. 
 Along with these injuries, Morant also faced certain issues in his performance. For instance, in the 2025-26 season, the 27-year-old played 20 games, averaging 19.5 points per game. However, Morant shooting percentages dropped to a career-low 41% from the field and 23% from beyond the arc. 
 Besides these issues, Morant also faced several off-court issues. The former Grizzlies star faced suspensions from the NBA in 2023 and even had a fallout with Grizzlies head coach Tuomas Lisalo last season. All these incidents eventually led to Morant’s trade to the Trail Blazers, where the two-time NBA All-Star looks to reset his career. 
 Ja Morant Has Been Decent So Far For Portland Trail Blazers
 Morant hasn’t taken too long to fit in a new culture with the Trail Blazers. In the three games so far this season, the 27-year-old has been an outright starter for the franchise. The former Grizzlies star is slowly getting into his own on the court as well. 
 Morant is just averaging 16.3 points and 6.3 assists per game. Yet despite that, the two-time NBA All-Star has looked pretty good and is scoring 58.8% from the field and 44.4% from downtown. Besides, these numbers are also bound to go up as the season progresses. 
 Morant's partnership with Damian Lillard in the backcourt is one of the most touted in the NBA this season. Behind them, the Trail Blazers are currently 3-0 in the Northwest Division. But they face a Memphis Grizzlies team that is also coming into this game following a 4-0 run, setting the stage for a promising contest at the Moda Center on Thursday.
